newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiichi Pharm cancer drug linked to 24 dead -paper.
newsitem.headline: Daiichi Pharm cancer drug linked to 24 dead -paper.

text.p: At least 24 people who were treated with the anti-cancer drug irinotecan hydrochloride, sold by Daiichi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd, died due to symptoms believed to be linked to side effects of the drug, a Japanese daily said on Tuesday.
Daiichi started selling the drug in April 1994 and it had been used by about 3,100 patients by March 1997, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Daiichi spokesmen were not immediately available for comment on the report.
Daiichi provided the number of the deaths to a hospital which had asked the Ministry of Health and Welfare for information about the drug's side effects, the newspaper report said.
The ministry released information in 1995 on deaths believed linked to the drug but has not made any further announcements, the newspaper said.
The other information held by the ministry included further deaths and details on the patients' use of the drug, it said.
The drug has also been sold by Yakult Honsha Co Ltd since April 1994 but data on the use of the drug sold by Yakult was not available, the paper said.
Yakult spokesmen were not available for comment.
